{
  "summary": "The draft is completely blank — no title, description, roster or premise — so any quality set I invent now would be a guess at the wrong story and would have to be torn out. Three quick questions pin down the genre, the protagonist's stance, and which dramatic currency the gates should actually read, and then I'll propose the full quality set (plus latching/monotonic/roll choices) in one pass.",
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "premise",
      "text": "What's the story? One line on the situation the player is dropped into.",
      "why": "Genre and situation decide whether the tracked currencies are trust, peril, evidence, sanity, or something else entirely.",
      "options": [
        "Fantasy quest into dangerous ruins",
        "Sci-fi survival / stranded crew",
        "Noir or detective mystery",
        "Court intrigue / political drama",
        "Romance or slice-of-life character drama",
        "You decide"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "protagonist",
      "text": "Who does the player play, and what do they want badly enough to act on?",
      "why": "The protagonist's want becomes the spine of the anchor objectives and the monotonic progress quality.",
      "options": [
        "An outsider hired into a group that doesn't trust them",
        "A leader responsible for people who depend on them",
        "An investigator hunting a truth someone wants buried",
        "A local tied to the place, resisting an intruder or an occupation",
        "You decide"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "currency",
      "text": "Which dramatic currencies should the extractor actually read from the prose? Pick the two or three that matter most.",
      "why": "Each currency becomes one extractor quality with a yes/no or short-answer rubric; extras dilute the gates.",
      "options": [
        "Trust/rapport with one key character (monotonic up)",
        "External danger level in the current scene (calm → critical)",
        "Progress toward the concrete goal (monotonic up)",
        "What the protagonist has learned / evidence gathered",
        "A latching decision: has the protagonist committed to a side or an oath",
        "You decide"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
